hypothesis: A warp can load a 4×32 input strip with adjacent lanes reading adjacent columns, then transpose four-lane subtiles by exchanging the two low lane bits with two register-index bits using only width-4, same-warp shuffles. This reduces values and shuffle stages per thread compared with the selected 16×16-subgroup parent, but requires eight warps per 32×32 tile and writes in four-float segments, so the store transactions or added warps may outweigh the reduced per-thread work.
notes: Historical controller n=1024 samples (not measurements of this proposal): selected parent 51ce1da6ff424257: 3.41472006403e-6, 3.39040020481e-6, 3.34111996926e-6 seconds (mean 3.382080079366667e-6); 5c066fd51f984909: 3.33503982984e-6, 3.49024008028e-6, 3.45151987858e-6 seconds (mean 3.4255999295666667e-6); 1a4f3ff518c24ac0: 3.71679989621e-6, 3.95839987323e-6, 3.82304005325e-6 seconds (mean 3.832746607563334e-6). The baseline mean was 1.6919040431599998e-5 seconds. The supplied context does not establish whether those sample timings are full-run rather than protected-kernel timings. This proposal has no controller timing or register/spill evidence yet; await the ordinary build output and repeated n=1024 measurements before drawing a performance conclusion.
transformations: Changed ownership to eight warps per 32×32 tile, with each warp loading a 4×32 strip and each lane holding four input-row values for one column.
Transposed 4×4 subtiles by swapping two register-index bits and two low lane bits through width-4 warp-local XOR shuffles; no cross-warp shuffle, shared-memory staging, or CTA barrier is used.
Stored bit-preserved unsigned float representations to output using size_t offsets; retained the run entry point and 32×32 grid coverage for positive n divisible by 32.
